perspective:
From Gloria’s perspective, here is what she has access to:

- She works with Donald at a large event planning company; she is an administrative assistant, and he bartends part-time during events. They mostly interact at company events and aren’t personally close.
- Over several company events, she directly observed Donald looking distracted and unenthusiastic while serving drinks.
- She approached him and said she noticed he seemed “off” lately, and asked if everything was okay with the job. Donald told her he wasn’t as into it as he used to be and that it felt “repetitive.”
- After thinking about their talk, she suggested that work dissatisfaction might sometimes reflect deeper personal issues and asked if he had considered talking to a professional. Donald said he hadn’t considered it and wasn’t sure it would help.
- After that conversation, she sensed a change in Donald’s behavior toward her and worried he might resent her suggestion as overstepping. She apologized, saying she only wanted to help because she cared. Donald told her he was “a bit taken aback at first” but knew she meant well, and that it was “a lot to process.”
- She felt relieved that the tension had eased and decided to strengthen their working relationship. She told Donald about an upcoming project and invited his creative input. He thanked her, said he’d like to be more involved, and called it a great opportunity.
- After they collaborated successfully, she observed Donald’s significant contributions and renewed enthusiasm, and she concluded he was a valuable team member. In a team meeting, she publicly acknowledged his work, saying his efforts were crucial to the project’s success. Donald thanked her and said it meant a lot to him, that he was glad to contribute, and that it felt good to be appreciated.
final_response:
In scenario 5, after seeing Donald’s renewed enthusiasm and valuable contributions, Gloria publicly acknowledged his work in a team meeting. Her intention was to recognize his efforts and make sure he felt appreciated and valued as part of the team.
